Maria: Hey — noticed generator stream doesn't stop when request context cancels in our sampleapp. Quick repro:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
resp, _ := client.Generator().Generate(ctx, req)
// resp.Stream() never returns even after ctx.Done()
```
Anyone seen this?

Jon: Hmm can you paste the minimal req? Also which SDK version?

Maria: Using go-sdk v0.3.1 and model 'redwood/gpt-small', sampleapp default prompt. Repro on mac and CI.

Sam: That sounds like the handshake goroutine is blocked on readFromConn during initial stream. We had a similar race where handshake isn't tied to ctx.

Kai: Yup. There's a known gap: handshake + token refresh run in separate goroutines and the generator stream goroutine waits on a channel that isn't closed on ctx cancel. Workaround: call resp.Close() from a goroutine after ctx.Done() or set a deadline on socket.

Maria: Ok workaround helps, but that's awkward for onboarding. Any ETA for a proper fix?

Jon: Filed issue #3242. Linking minimal fix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/789 — adds ctx propagation for handshake and ensures streamRead returns on ctx.Done()

devbot: deploy queued for staging: generator-handshake-ctx-prop (CI: passed)

Maria: Awesome, thanks. Can we add this pattern to the sampleapp with a comment? That would save new users.

Sam: Agreed — will push a tiny sample update and a short note in the README about using ctx with streaming and using resp.Close() as fallback. :thumbsup:
